newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shares end higher, chemical firm plunges.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shares end higher, chemical firm plunges.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in markets dominated by dealings in rarely-traded shares that have little impact on the leading price indices, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up a mere 0.04 percent to close at 13,255.66 on a trading volume of 1.52 billion pesos. Bogota rose 0.40 percent, however, ending at 836.66 on a lower-than-average volume of 620.4 million pesos.
"There was some movement in the markets today but there's still no definite trend, especially among the leading shares," one broker said in a telephone interview.
The day's biggest loser by far was Productos Quimicos Panamericana SA, a rarely-heard-of chemical manufacturer that plummeted 27 percent in Medellin to end at 151.62 pesos.
Nearly 900 million pesos of stock in the company traded hands in a move that brokers speculated had something to do with a possible buyout of the firm at previously agreed bargain basement prices.
Spokesmen for the company, Colombia's 34th largest chemical maker in terms of assets, could not be reached for immediate comment.
Winners in Medellin included steelmaker Siderugica de Medellin, which ended up 6.52 percent at 245 pesos a share, and engineering firm Distral, which closed up 9.19 percent at 24 pesos per share.

Gainers in Bogota were led blue-chip Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary shares closed up 1.21 percent at 250 pesos per share and Banco de Bogota, which closed up 1.91 percent at 5,850 pesos per share. Retail chain Cadenalco also ended higher, moving up 1.83 percent to close at 886 pesos per share.
